\(4x + 5y = 19\) \(\therefore 4(1) + 5y = 19\) \(\therefore 5y = 15\) \(\therefore y = 3\)

\(\therefore\) the correct alternative is the one whose value is 3.

\(x = \dfrac{49}{7} = 7\)

solution:
Write both equations in the form \(ax + by = c\): \(x + y = 3\) and \(3x - 2y = 4\).

D is the determinant of the coefficients of \(x\) and \(y\).

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = (1)(-2) - (1)(3) = -2 - 3 = -5\)

\(\therefore\) the correct alternative is the one whose value is \(-5\).

solution:
For \(ax + by = c\) and \(mx + ny = d\), the determinant of the coefficients is \(\mathrm{D} = an - bm\).

Given \(an \neq bm\), so \(\mathrm{D} \neq 0\), and Cramer's rule gives exactly one value of \(x\) and one value of \(y\).

Geometrically the two lines are neither parallel nor coincident, so they cut each other at exactly one point.

\(\therefore\) the equations have only one common solution.
